title: Joshua Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Joshua 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The children of Israel did so as Joshua commanded
Joshua said unto them, Pass over before the ark
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, indicating that the LORD spoke to Joshua after the people passed over Jordan.

questions.question: How many men did Joshua take from the people?
questions.explanation: Joshua commanded to take twelve men, one from each tribe, as stated in Joshua 4:2.

questions.question: What were the men commanded to take from the midst of Jordan?
questions.explanation: Joshua commanded them to take twelve stones out of the midst of Jordan, as stated in Joshua 4:3.

questions.question: Where were the stones to be laid down?
questions.explanation: The stones were to be taken to the lodging place, where they would stay that night, according to Joshua 4:3.

questions.question: What did Joshua instruct the men to carry on their shoulders?
questions.explanation: Joshua instructed each man to take up a stone upon his shoulder, as stated in Joshua 4:5.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the stones according to Joshua?
options: To remember the crossing of Jordan
To make a monument for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: To remember the crossing of Jordan
questions.explanation: The stones were to serve as a sign and a memorial for the children of Israel to remember the event of the Jordan being cut off, as mentioned in Joshua 4:7.

questions.question: What question were the children likely to ask about the stones?
options: What mean ye by these stones?
Where did these stones come from?
questions.correctAnswer: What mean ye by these stones?
questions.explanation: The children were expected to ask their fathers what the significance of the stones was, as stated in Joshua 4:6.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel do as Joshua commanded?
questions.explanation: The children of Israel followed Joshua's command and took up twelve stones from the midst of Jordan, as stated in Joshua 4:8.

questions.question: According to Joshua 4, who spoke to Joshua?
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that the LORD spoke to Joshua after the people crossed the Jordan, as stated in Joshua 4:1.

questions.question: How many tribes are represented by the stones?
questions.explanation: The stones were to correspond to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel, which is twelve, as stated in Joshua 4:5.

questions.question: The waters of Jordan were cut off before what?
questions.explanation: The waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, as mentioned in Joshua 4:7.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD commanded Joshua to take twelve men.
questions.explanation: This is true as the LORD spoke to Joshua and commanded him to take twelve men from the people, as stated in Joshua 4:2.

questions.question: True or False: The stones were to be a memorial for the children of Israel.
questions.explanation: This is true as the stones were meant to be a memorial for the children of Israel forever, according to Joshua 4:7.

questions.question: True or False: The stones were to be placed in the tabernacle.
questions.explanation: This is false; the stones were to be laid down in the lodging place, not in the tabernacle, as stated in Joshua 4:3.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua commanded the people to bring back fish from the Jordan.
questions.explanation: This is false; there is no mention of fish being involved in Joshua 4; the focus is on stones.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Joshua set up in the midst of Jordan?
questions.explanation: Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of Jordan as stated in Joshua 4:9.

questions.question: What does Joshua 4:10 promise will happen if the priests bear the ark as commanded?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:10 indicates that the priests stood in the midst of Jordan until everything was finished, which allowed the people to pass over.

questions.question: When did the ark of the LORD pass over?
questions.explanation: According to Joshua 4:11, the ark of the LORD passed over after all the people had clean passed over.

questions.question: What commands did Moses give regarding the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh?
options: To pass over armed before the others
questions.correctAnswer: To pass over armed before the others
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:12 states that the children of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh passed over armed as Moses commanded.

questions.question: How many prepared for war passed over before the LORD?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:13 mentions that about forty thousand prepared for war passed over before the LORD unto battle.

questions.question: What was the result of the LORD magnifying Joshua in the sight of Israel?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:14 states that the LORD magnified Joshua and the people feared him as they feared Moses.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Joshua to do after magnifying him?
options: Command the priests to come up out of Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: Command the priests to come up out of Jordan
questions.explanation: In Joshua 4:16, the LORD commanded Joshua to instruct the priests that bear the ark to come up out of Jordan.

questions.question: How can the memorial stones help future generations?
options: They can serve as a reminder of God's power
They can be used for building
questions.correctAnswer: They can serve as a reminder of God's power
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:7 explains that the stones are a memorial to tell future generations about how God cut off the waters of Jordan.

questions.question: What should the people do when their children ask about the stones?
questions.explanation: According to Joshua 4:6-7, they should answer that the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant.

questions.question: What was the significance of the priests standing in Jordan?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:10 shows that the priests' position in the Jordan represented their role in God's command and the people's crossing.

questions.question: What action reflects obedience in Joshua 4?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:11 indicates that the people passed over as commanded, demonstrating their obedience.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about leadership?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:14 shows that Joshua was magnified as a leader, indicating that leaders have a significant impact on the obedience of their followers.

questions.question: Is it true that the stones were intended to be a permanent memorial?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:7 states that the stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel forever.

questions.question: Is it false that the children of Israel did not obey Joshua's command?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:8 indicates that the children of Israel did as Joshua commanded, showing their obedience.

questions.question: Is it false that the ark of the LORD was ignored during the crossing?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:11 shows that the ark of the LORD played a crucial role during the crossing, indicating it was not ignored.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 4.

questions.question: What did Joshua command the priests to do after they came up out of Jordan?
options: Come ye up out of Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: Come ye up out of Jordan
questions.explanation: Joshua commanded the priests to 'Come ye up out of Jordan' as stated in Joshua 4:17.

questions.question: What happened when the priests' feet were lifted up onto the dry land?
questions.explanation: The verse states that when the priests lifted their feet to the dry land, 'the waters of Jordan returned unto their place' (Joshua 4:18).

questions.question: On which day of the month did the people come up out of Jordan?
options: Tenth day of the first month
questions.correctAnswer: Tenth day of the first month
questions.explanation: According to Joshua 4:19, the people came up out of Jordan on the 'tenth day of the first month'.

questions.question: Where did Joshua set up the twelve stones taken from Jordan?
questions.explanation: Joshua pitched the twelve stones in Gilgal as stated in Joshua 4:20.

questions.question: What should the children of Israel tell their children when they ask about the stones?
options: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land
questions.correctAnswer: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land
questions.explanation: The children of Israel were to let their children know that 'Israel came over this Jordan on dry land' (Joshua 4:22).

questions.question: Why did the Lord dry up the waters of Jordan?
questions.explanation: The purpose was 'that all the people of the earth might know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty' (Joshua 4:24).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'מַצָּב' (matzav) in Joshua 4:20 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'מַצָּב' (matzav) can mean a memorial or standing structure, which relates to the context of the stones set up.

questions.question: Which literary technique is exemplified in the phrase 'the waters of Jordan were cut off'?
questions.explanation: The phrase reflects a form of parallelism by contrasting the actions of the waters and the ark.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of crossing a body of water?
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:21 describes God parting the Red Sea, similar to the crossing of the Jordan in Joshua 4.

questions.question: Which other passage in the New Testament reflects on God's mighty acts as in Joshua 4?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:22 references the mighty works of Jesus as a fulfillment of God's power, resonating with the theme in Joshua 4.

questions.question: What precedes the command for the priests to come up out of Jordan?
questions.explanation: The command follows after noting that 'all the people were clean passed over Jordan' (Joshua 4:1).

questions.question: Which event occurs immediately after the priests come up out of Jordan?
questions.explanation: After the priests came up out of Jordan, 'the waters of Jordan returned unto their place' (Joshua 4:18).

questions.question: The act of setting up stones in Gilgal serves as a memorial for what reason?
options: To show the might of God
questions.correctAnswer: To show the might of God
questions.explanation: The stones serve as a reminder of God's power in parting the waters, as expressed in Joshua 4:24.

questions.question: The statement 'that ye might fear the LORD your God for ever' is intended to convey what?
questions.explanation: This statement emphasizes the reason for the miraculous act, as stated in Joshua 4:24.

questions.question: Joshua's command to gather stones was meant for immediate personal use only.
questions.explanation: The stones were gathered for a lasting memorial for future generations, as explained in Joshua 4:6.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Joshua 4:7 teach about God's nature in relation to His acts of salvation?
options: God's acts of salvation serve as eternal memorials to His covenant faithfulness
God's salvation is temporary and intended only for the generation experiencing it
God's power is limited by human memory and tradition
God's salvation depends on human works for its efficacy
questions.correctAnswer: God's acts of salvation serve as eternal memorials to His covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:7 explains that the stones are to be a memorial "unto the children of Israel for ever," showing that God's salvific acts are eternally significant and remembered as signs of His covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providence is taught in Joshua 4:18 regarding the restoration of the Jordan's waters?
options: God sovereignly controls natural elements to accomplish His redemptive purposes
God acts randomly without purpose in natural events
God's providence is limited to spiritual matters, not physical creation
God's control over nature is symbolic but not actual
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls natural elements to accomplish His redemptive purposes
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:18 describes how the waters of Jordan returned "as they did before" only after the priests left the riverbed, demonstrating God's sovereign orchestration of nature to fulfill His covenantal promises.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s covenant faithfulness is evident in Joshua 4:23 when comparing the crossing of Jordan to the Red Sea?
options: God consistently fulfills His promises by repeating salvific acts for His people
God's acts of salvation are unique and will never be repeated
God's covenant is conditional on Israel's perfect obedience
God's saving acts are only for Moses' generation
questions.correctAnswer: God consistently fulfills His promises by repeating salvific acts for His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:23 explicitly compares God's drying up of the Jordan to the Red Sea event, showing His consistent covenant faithfulness across different generations to deliver His people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Joshua 4:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:14 declares that "the LORD magnified Joshua" in the sight of Israel, demonstrating God's sovereign power to exalt leaders according to His purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Joshua 4:24?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:24 states that "all the people of the earth might know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty," emphasizing God’s attribute of mightiness.

questions.question: How does Joshua 4:20 connect the crossing of Jordan to the theme of covenant remembrance in the Old Testament?
options: By setting up memorial stones at Gilgal to remind Israel of God's deliverance
By establishing a new temple at Gilgal for sacrifice
By commanding Israel to forget past miracles to focus on obedience
By calling for a permanent cessation of stone monuments
questions.correctAnswer: By setting up memorial stones at Gilgal to remind Israel of God's deliverance
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:20 records Joshua pitching the twelve stones at Gilgal, linking the physical memorial to covenant remembrance, a recurring theme in Israel’s history (cf. Exodus 12:14).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Joshua 4:13 illustrate by mentioning the armed crossing before the Lord to battle?
options: God’s enabling of His people to conquer the promised land through divine empowerment
Israel’s military might as their ultimate source of victory
The necessity of human wisdom over divine guidance
The replacement of God’s power with political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: God’s enabling of His people to conquer the promised land through divine empowerment
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:13 highlights the prepared warriors crossing "before the LORD unto battle," connecting divine empowerment to Israel’s conquest, a key theme in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Joshua 4:6 and Joshua 4:21 teach about the function of memorials in the life of God’s people?
options: Memorials serve as means of teaching future generations about God’s saving acts
Memorials are merely decorative with no theological purpose
Memorials replace the need for written Scripture
Memorials are a form of idolatry and must be avoided
questions.correctAnswer: Memorials serve as means of teaching future generations about God’s saving acts
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that stones serve as signs prompting questions from children, enabling the transmission of knowledge regarding God's salvific acts to future generations.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Joshua 4:15 and Joshua 4:16 about God’s communication with His leaders?
options: God gives direct, authoritative commands to fulfill His covenant promises
God communicates only through dreams and visions
God’s guidance is always indirect and vague
God requires leaders to act without any revelation
questions.correctAnswer: God gives direct, authoritative commands to fulfill His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:15-16 shows God speaking directly to Joshua, commanding the priests, illustrating God’s active and clear guidance of His covenant leaders.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God’s providential timing is taught by Joshua 4:10 and Joshua 4:11?
options: God’s providence perfectly coordinates events to fulfill His commands
God’s timing is accidental and unrelated to His will
Human action causes God’s providence to fail
God’s providence delays fulfillment until human perfection
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence perfectly coordinates events to fulfill His commands
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 describe priests standing until everything was finished and then the ark crossing, showing God’s precise timing to accomplish His purposes.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Joshua 4:1-9 teaches that the miraculous crossing of the Jordan was a natural event exaggerated by propaganda. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The passage records a supernatural act of God stopping the river's flow to demonstrate His power
The event was a normal river crossing with no divine intervention
The stones were simply a commemorative art project with no miracle involved
The event is a myth with no historical basis
questions.correctAnswer: The passage records a supernatural act of God stopping the river's flow to demonstrate His power
questions.explanation: Verses 1-9 describe God stopping the Jordan and the priests standing in the riverbed, indicating a miraculous act demonstrating God's power, not mere natural crossing.

questions.question: What doctrine about human obedience and divine command is taught in Joshua 4:8?
options: Obedience to God's commands is essential for covenant faithfulness and blessing
Human obedience is irrelevant to God’s plans
God’s commands are suggestions rather than requirements
Obedience is replaced by human wisdom and initiative
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands is essential for covenant faithfulness and blessing
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:8 states that Israel did "as Joshua commanded," showing that faithful obedience to God's instructions is necessary for covenant relationship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Joshua 4:19 when the people encamped at Gilgal after crossing the Jordan?
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:19 records the people encamping at Gilgal as part of God’s faithfulness in leading them into the promised land.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made in Joshua 4:22 between the crossing of Jordan and Israel's salvation history?
options: The crossing is a typological fulfillment of God’s saving acts, reinforcing trust in His power
The crossing was a new event unrelated to past salvation history
The crossing replaced the Passover as Israel’s primary salvation event
The crossing diminished the significance of the Red Sea event
questions.correctAnswer: The crossing is a typological fulfillment of God’s saving acts, reinforcing trust in His power
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:22 calls the crossing of the Jordan on dry land, paralleling the Red Sea, thus typologically reinforcing God's saving power throughout Israel’s history.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of priesthood in covenant mediation is conveyed in Joshua 4:9?
options: Priests function as mediators standing in God’s presence during covenant acts
Priests have no special role in covenant events
Priests are symbolic figures with no real spiritual function
Priests replace the people as the covenant recipients
questions.correctAnswer: Priests function as mediators standing in God’s presence during covenant acts
questions.explanation: Joshua 4:9 describes the priests standing in the Jordan at the ark, symbolizing their mediatory role in God's covenantal interaction with Israel.
